title: Logged model search order by metric: pagination needs exactly one latest metric row per model (row_number, not rank)
answers: Why does paging through logged models sorted by a metric return the same model more than once?
Logged model search ordered by metrics.<name> with tied dataset metrics shows duplicate models across pages, how is that fixed?
Where is the metric ordering for search_logged_models with order_by handled?
How does the latest metric value per logged model get chosen when sorting by a metric?
body:
Path: Logged-model search (search_logged_models with order_by on metrics.<name>, used by paginated logged-model lists) passes through mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore._apply_order_by_search_logged_models, which builds a per-model subquery of logged model metric rows and outer-joins it into the ORDER BY.
Rule: Keep one row per model_id in that subquery by using row_number() (filtered to row_num == 1), not rank(). rank() keeps every tied row, so ties across datasets duplicated the model before pagination. The window ORDER BY is metric_timestamp_ms desc, metric_step desc, then run_id asc as a deterministic tie-breaker.
Symptom: A logged model sorted by a metric appeared several times in the result set when its latest metric rows tied across datasets (for example train/val/test with the same value), so paginated listings repeated models.
Constraints: Applies only to metric-based ordering in search_logged_models. run_id asc only makes the choice deterministic; it does not define a meaningful preference between datasets. Non-metric order keys are not affected by this subquery.
applies: SQL tracking store, search_logged_models ordering by metric values with pagination (max_results / page_token).
says: Paging through models sorted by metric displays the same model multiple times.
Models with identical scores across datasets appear repeatedly when browsing sorted model lists.
Stop duplicate model entries from showing up when sorting models by an evaluation metric.
Sorting the logged models list by score causes duplicate entries across pages.
search: SqlAlchemyStore._apply_order_by_search_logged_models must filter metric subqueries using row_number() equal to 1 instead of rank() when sorting logged models by a metric. Using rank() retained tied rows across datasets such as train and test, causing duplicate models to appear across paginated search_logged_models results. The ordering subquery breaks ties using metric_timestamp_ms desc, metric_step desc, and run_id asc, applying only to metric-based ordering in the SQL tracking store.
